stem: A job should start as soon as an upstream table is written, but the team also wants a nightly safety net in case that write never happens. They are checking whether one job can carry both arrangements at once.

option_texts.A: Several can be added, and a run starts when any active one evaluates to true
option_texts.B: Only one arrangement is allowed, so the safety net needs a second job
option_texts.C: Several can be added, but a run starts only when all of them agree
option_texts.D: Only one arrangement is allowed unless the job is set to run continuously

drill_answer_short: A job can carry multiple triggers; when any active trigger evaluates to true it starts a run
decision_hinge: You can add multiple triggers of the same or different types to a job, and when any active trigger evaluates to true it starts a run, for example a table update trigger plus an additional scheduled trigger as a backup.

plausible_options.B: wants a nightly safety net in case that write never happens

eliminated_by.C: should start as soon as an upstream table is written
eliminated_by.D: checking whether one job can carry both arrangements at once

distractor_traps.B: T5: common misconception - a second job is unnecessary because triggers combine on one job
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - requiring agreement would defeat a backup that fires when the first never does
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - continuous running is unrelated to how many triggers a job may hold

stem: An on-call rota wants to hear about a job that is merely running far longer than usual, well before it has either finished or failed. The team is checking whether the built-in alerting can express that at all.

option_texts.A: No, alerting fires only once a run has reached a finished or failed state
option_texts.B: Yes, there is an event for a run whose duration exceeds a configured threshold
option_texts.C: Yes, but only by polling the run history from an outside scheduler
option_texts.D: No, a long run has to be caught by a separate watchdog job

drill_answer_short: Notification events include start, success, failure, and a duration exceeding a configured threshold
decision_hinge: You can set up notifications on runs of a job and individual job tasks for Start, Successful completion, Failure, the duration exceeds a configured threshold, and a streaming backlog metric exceeds a configured threshold.

plausible_options.C: wants to hear about a job that is merely running far longer than usual

eliminated_by.A: well before it has either finished or failed
eliminated_by.D: checking whether the built-in alerting can express that at all

distractor_traps.A: T5: common misconception - start and duration events both fire before a run resolves
distractor_traps.C: T2: scope error - an outside poller is the workaround the built-in event removes
distractor_traps.D: T3: confusable sibling - a watchdog would work but duplicates a shipped feature

stem: A downstream job starts whenever an upstream job completes, and one morning the upstream finishes twice while the downstream is still busy with an earlier run. The team must say what happened to the second completion.

option_texts.A: It started a parallel run, because completion is not subject to the concurrency cap
option_texts.B: It was skipped, exactly as an overlapping schedule would have been skipped
option_texts.C: It was retained until another run could start, because completions are held
option_texts.D: It was discarded and recorded as an error against the upstream job

drill_answer_short: Job completion triggers retain ready completions until another run can start, unlike most trigger types which are skipped
decision_hinge: Runs from most trigger types are skipped when they exceed the configured max concurrency for a job, but job completion triggers retain ready completions until another run can start.

plausible_options.B: the upstream finishes twice while the downstream is still busy with an earlier run

eliminated_by.A: A downstream job starts whenever an upstream job completes
eliminated_by.D: The team must say what happened to the second completion

distractor_traps.A: T5: common misconception - the concurrency cap still applies, which is why the completion waits
distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - that is the behaviour of most trigger types, but completion triggers are the exception
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - a held completion is not an error on the upstream job

stem: A join matches each event timestamp against a table of validity windows, and it runs far slower than an equality join of the same size. The team is identifying which optimization applies to a condition shaped this way.

option_texts.A: Skew handling, because matching against windows concentrates work on a few tasks
option_texts.B: Broadcast, because a condition of this shape always has one tiny side
option_texts.C: Partition pruning, an optimization that skips whole files at read time
option_texts.D: The range join optimization, for a point in interval or interval overlap condition

drill_answer_short: Range join optimization applies to point-in-interval or interval-overlap conditions and uses a bin size
decision_hinge: The range join optimization applies to a query that has a point in interval or interval overlap range join condition, and has a bin size, either derived automatically or specified manually.

plausible_options.A: it runs far slower than an equality join of the same size

eliminated_by.B: A join matches each event timestamp against a table of validity windows
eliminated_by.C: identifying which optimization applies to a condition shaped this way

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - skew is a distribution problem, where this is the join condition's shape
distractor_traps.B: T5: common misconception - nothing about an interval condition implies a small side
distractor_traps.C: T2: scope error - pruning depends on the layout of the table, not on the join condition
